# Counter and motion-graphic usage

**Which motion graphics carry information?** · [all approaches](index.md)


## None or minimal
<a id="none"></a>

Footage and captions only.

**Looks like:** Real footage carries everything; at most a title card. Feels natural and documentary.

**Good at:** speed; authenticity; nothing to build

**Weak at:** numbers and steps are harder to follow; less to look at in teaching reels

**Best for:** formats reel30, story, yt-long, podcast · niches travel, gym, all · goals speed, trust · effort low

**How:** Captions only in Edits.

**Backed by:** [Podcast body: long takes, demos as interrupts](../topics/editing.md#edit-podcast-long-takes), [Hard cuts; motion only on overlays](../topics/transitions.md#tr-hard-cuts-motion-on-overlays), [Nothing linear](../topics/effects.md#fx-nothing-linear), [Untangle: hook, format, topic, illustration](../topics/growth.md#growth-untangle-data), [Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example) · sources L08, L06

## Counters and progress badges
<a id="counters-badges"></a>

Numbers count up (weights, prices, stars) and n/3 badges mark list items.

**Looks like:** '75 KG' ticks up from 0 as the bar moves; 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 badges in the corner. The viewer always knows where they are.

**Good at:** retention; makes numbers feel big; list structure

**Weak at:** gimmicky if every reel has one; build time per counter

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches gym, tech, all · goals retention, saves · effort medium

**How:** HyperFrames counter component; CapCut number templates.

**Backed by:** [Animated number counters](../topics/effects.md#fx-number-counter), [n/3 progress badges in list videos](../topics/effects.md#fx-progress-badges), [Challenge, ranking and list templates](../topics/hooks.md#l11-classic-hook-templates), [Track only metrics that change actions](../topics/growth.md#growth-track-few-metrics) · sources L02, R1

## Data cards, stamps and price strikes
<a id="data-cards"></a>

Parts grids that fill up, receipts, date stamps, price strike-throughs, DON'T BUY stamps, SAVED pills.

**Looks like:** An empty parts grid fills slot by slot with prices while a budget bar grows; the old price is struck through and the new one lands with a stamp.

**Good at:** proof; saves; comparisons

**Weak at:** design time; prices go stale

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, carousel · niches tech, gaming · goals saves, trust · effort high

**How:** HyperFrames price cards and charts; CapCut shapes plus text.

**Backed by:** [Live-build parts card with budget bar](../topics/effects.md#fx-live-build-parts-card), [Price strikes, stamps, pills and ticks](../topics/effects.md#fx-price-strike-through), [Date-stamped prices](../topics/text.md#text-date-stamped-prices), [Frosted cards, drawn diagrams, red arrows](../topics/effects.md#fx-frosted-glass-cards), [UI and text pops: spring with slight overshoot](../topics/effects.md#fx-spring-ui) · sources R1

## Proof cards on the exact word
<a id="proof-cards-on-word"></a>

Screenshots, repo cards and logo cards appear the moment they are named; real screenshots over mock-ups.

**Looks like:** You say 'Whisper' and the GitHub card pops above your head on that syllable, with a highlighter on the key line.

**Good at:** trust; precision; tutorials

**Weak at:** needs word timing; screenshots to gather

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long · niches tech · goals trust, saves · effort medium

**How:** faster-whisper word timestamps, then HyperFrames cards placed on those times.

**Backed by:** [Tool card lands on the word](../topics/text.md#l10-card-on-the-word), [Show proof on screen](../topics/editing.md#edit-proof-inserts), [Real screenshot beats an AI mock-up](../topics/editing.md#l10-real-screenshot-not-mockup), [Word-level transcription for captions and cuts](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-word-level-transcription), [Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example) · sources L10, R1, L07

## Signature effects: text behind head, B&W freeze, memes
<a id="signature-effects"></a>

A few recurring tricks that become part of the look.

**Looks like:** The title sits behind your head; a sarcastic line freezes in black and white; a 2 s meme cutaway has the product pasted in.

**Good at:** recognition; humour; covers

**Weak at:** wears out if overused; the cut-out needs good separation

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches all · goals retention, shares · effort medium

**How:** Segmentation cut-out (CapCut auto cut-out or HyperFrames), a desaturate-and-hold freeze, meme overlays.

**Backed by:** [Text behind your head](../topics/effects.md#l10-text-behind-head), [B&W freeze for sarcastic punchlines](../topics/effects.md#fx-bw-freeze-punchline), [Meme cutaways with the product pasted in](../topics/editing.md#edit-meme-cutaways), [Covers: payoff frame, number, face, accent](../topics/text.md#text-cover-meme-payoff), [UI and text pops: spring with slight overshoot](../topics/effects.md#fx-spring-ui) · sources L10, R1

## Mixing
Rahul uses counters, data cards and signature effects in one reel. L10 uses proof cards plus one signature effect (text behind the head) reused for the CTA.

## Rule of thumb
Numbers and lists: counters. Prices and builds: data cards. Tutorials: proof cards. Brand recognition: one signature effect.
